# Checkpoint research schema

Two checkpoints. An item belongs to the checkpoint at which a PM could have known it (source published on or before the cut-off):

| checkpoint | cut-off | typical period covered |
|---|---|---|
| `2026-01` | published ≤ 2026-01-31 | FY2025, Q4 2025, Dec 2025, forecasts for 2026 made in Dec/Jan |
| `2026-07` | published 2026-02-01 … 2026-07-31 | H1 2026, Q2 2026, Jun 2026, mid-year forecast revisions |

Anything published after 2026-07-31 is out (do not record it).

Each raw file `raw/<topic>.json`:

```json
{
  "topic": "<topic>",
  "retrieved_at": "2026-10-11",
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "kebab-case-unique-id",
      "checkpoint": "2026-01 | 2026-07",
      "kind": "metric | event | trend | study | policy",
      "region": "GLOBAL | EU | DE | UK | US | CN | JP | KR",
      "entity": "market | <brand> | <brand model>",
      "segment": "compact_premium | executive | luxury | premium_all | mass | all | null",
      "powertrain": "BEV | PHEV | EREV | HEV | ICE | all | null",
      "metric": "deliveries | registrations | retail_sales | market_share | bev_share | nev_share | yoy | price | rating | survey_share | other | null",
      "period_covered": "FY2025 | Q4-2025 | Dec-2025 | H1-2026 | Q2-2026 | Jun-2026 | ...",
      "value": 123456,
      "unit": "units | pct | usd | eur | cny | km | kw | points | null",
      "yoy_pct": -12.5,
      "headline": "<= 12 words, plain",
      "driver": "<= 30 words: why it happened, as stated by the source (not your opinion)",
      "customer_relevance": "<= 25 words: what it suggests for premium car buyers' needs (this is an assumption)",
      "pair_key": "same string for the matching item at the other checkpoint, e.g. 'mercedes-cn-deliveries'",
      "source": { "url": "...", "publisher": "...", "published_at": "YYYY-MM-DD", "trust_tier": "T1 | T2 | T3" },
      "quote": "verbatim snippet from the page (<= 300 chars) that contains the value/claim",
      "verified": true,
      "notes": "conflicts with other sources, definitions (e.g. EU vs EU+EFTA+UK), caveats"
    }
  ],
  "gaps": ["what you searched for and could not find with a citable source"]
}
```

Trust tiers: T1 = OEM press releases / annual or quarterly reports, registration statistics (ACEA, KBA, SMMT, CPCA, CAAM, Cox/KBB for US); T2 = Reuters, Bloomberg, Automotive News, CnEVPost, Gasgoo, J.D. Power, McKinsey, Deloitte, S&P Global Mobility, Consumer Reports; T3 = blogs, forums, aggregators.

Rules: never invent a number; `verified: true` only if you fetched the page and the quote is on it; prefer T1; when sources disagree, record both and say so in `notes`; record a matching item at the other checkpoint (same `pair_key`) whenever one exists so the two periods can be compared.

150:| **5 Series / i5** | "Business athlete": dynamics plus long-distance comfort, top ADAS on the highway, fast charging and range, rear comfort in the China LWB, quiet cabin | China-only rear "boss" features in the G68 (pass for CN, warn for EU/US); third-party cockpit OS (CN only) | Sacrificing handling for float-ride everywhere; global commitment to an EREV range-extender identity **(PM judgement)** |
151:| **7 Series / i7** | Driver-*and*-chauffeur duality, Theatre Screen and rear lounge, Executive Lounge seats, craftsmanship, quiet BEV, L2+/L3 assisted driving | Matching Maextro/M9 gadgets one-for-one (fridge, projector) unless executed at BMW quality | Overt bling with no taste (grille-size controversy); dropping driving dynamics entirely (the S-Class owns pure comfort) |

CREATE TABLE source_item (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    kind TEXT NOT NULL,           -- feedback | study | sales | option_list | web | reference
    ref TEXT NOT NULL,            -- provenance: e.g. 'G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx#Feedback_Explorer:G60-0001'
    external_id TEXT,             -- e.g. verbatim ID G60-0001
    trust_tier TEXT,              -- T1..T3
    vehicle_model_id TEXT REFERENCES vehicle_model(id), market_code TEXT REFERENCES market(code),
    country TEXT, platform_id TEXT REFERENCES platform(id),
    url TEXT, published_at TEXT, retrieved_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now')),
    text TEXT, quote TEXT, meta_json TEXT,
    ingest_batch_id INTEGER REFERENCES ingest_batch(id), wave INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, checkpoint TEXT,
    UNIQUE (kind, ref)
);
CREATE INDEX ix_source_scope ON source_item(vehicle_model_id, market_code);
CREATE TABLE study_metric (           -- one row per study item × model × market (D-026)
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, source_item_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES source_item(id),
    vehicle_model_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES vehicle_model(id), market_code TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES market(code),
    item TEXT NOT NULL,           -- category / question text as in the file
    scale TEXT NOT NULL,          -- mean_10 (CN/EU means) | dist_7 (US 7-point distribution)
    mean REAL, top2 REAL, bottom3 REAL, net REAL,
    z_within_column REAL,         -- standardized vs. the other items of the same model × market column
    rank_within_column INTEGER, n_items_in_column INTEGER
);
CREATE TABLE req_area (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, key TEXT NOT NULL, run_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES checkpoint_run(id),
    title TEXT NOT NULL, need TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL,      -- improve | keep | emerging | quality
    theme_keys_json TEXT NOT NULL, why_now TEXT, open_questions_json TEXT, metrics_json TEXT,
    change_note TEXT, model TEXT, created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now')),
    UNIQUE (run_id, key)
);
CREATE TABLE source_aspect (
    source_item_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES source_item(id),
    key TEXT NOT NULL,                 -- study item label, research ref or option id
    aspect TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT,
    method TEXT NOT NULL,              -- luna | rule
    PRIMARY KEY (source_item_id, key)
);
CREATE TABLE evidence_edge (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, run_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES checkpoint_run(id),
    src_type TEXT NOT NULL, src_id TEXT NOT NULL, dst_type TEXT NOT NULL, dst_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    relation TEXT NOT NULL,     -- belongs_to | duplicate_of | sub_need_of | supports | contradicts | context |
                                -- competes_with | trend_for | available_as_option | derived_from | recalibrates
    weight REAL, method TEXT NOT NULL, rationale TEXT, model TEXT,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now'))
);
CREATE INDEX edge_run ON evidence_edge(run_id, dst_type, dst_id);

1:"""Stage `elicit` (D-043): themes + evidence graph → potential (candidate) requirements, per checkpoint.
4:Code checks (no LLM): themes that are only quality issues go to the quality hand-over; `at_successor_launch` needs a
5:dated trend/competitor edge, otherwise the horizon is set back to `today` and the gap is written as an assumption;
6:cited evidence ids must be among the theme's own edges; a market target without evidence from that market is
34:    title TEXT NOT NULL, statement TEXT, decision_type TEXT, today_status TEXT, horizon TEXT, horizon_year INTEGER,
35:    kano TEXT, detail_json TEXT, model TEXT,
42:class Metric(BaseModel):
43:    name: str
44:    unit: str
45:    method: str = Field(description="How it would be measured at launch")
48:class Target(BaseModel):
49:    line: Literal["1 Series", "5 Series", "7 Series"]
50:    market: Literal["EU", "US", "CN", "RoW"]
51:    rationale: str = Field(description="Why this car × market needs it, ≤ 25 words")
52:    evidence_ids: list[str]
55:class Draft(BaseModel):
56:    theme_key: str
57:    title: str = Field(description="≤ 10 words, the decision, not the problem")
58:    statement: str = Field(description="What the successor car should offer, as one product decision")
59:    decision_type: Literal["add_feature", "raise_capability", "change_design", "keep_strength", "package_variant", "market_variant"]
60:    today_status: Literal["standard", "optional", "package", "not_offered", "unknown"]
61:    metric: Metric
62:    targets: list[Target]
63:    horizon: Literal["today", "at_successor_launch"]
64:    horizon_year: int | None
65:    kano: Literal["basic", "performance", "delighter"]
66:    evidence_ids: list[str] = Field(description="ids from the theme's evidence list that support this candidate")

## 1. What BMW asks for (`/Users/atahankilic/Documents/ehl-munich-final/foundation/documents/challenge-brief.md`)

**Reference process, step 3 (image_2, lines ~70-75):**
> "**Requirements definition** — specification & quantification: measurable targets + acceptance criteria (e.g. "Range: 600 or 700 mi?", "Cooler for how many bottles?", "Seat ventilation: fast enough?"), grouped by Exterior / Interior / Powertrain / Driver assistance / … (AI + human)"

- Step 2 comes before it. It produces a "list of all potential requirements (0/1: implement?), e.g. BEV powertrain, cooler, seat ventilation". Step 4 follows it: "**Prioritization** — Customer, Business, … dimensions. (AI + human)". Step 5 is Documentation / tracking, drawn as a cycle.
- The definition the brief works from: "Customer Requirement = Customer-relevant attribute of a car." Requirements must be "clear, actionable, customer-facing, realistic", and the app "Must make clear what is evidence vs. forward-looking assumption".
- The deliverable list contains **no explicit "metric/target/acceptance criteria" field**. It asks for: ID, description, linked findings/sources, priority/score, prioritization rationale, evidence level, future-facing assumptions and uncertainties, and decision status. Measurable targets therefore come only from the process image.
- **Scope, In:** "range & charging *as experienced by the customer*", plus comfort, space, infotainment, driving experience, variants and packages.
- **Scope, Out:** "technical/engineering (component specs, architecture, suppliers)", regulatory/homologation/safety, and pricing/business case. "rough cost/effort as a prioritization factor is OK".
- **How this squares with "measurable targets":** targets have to be stated as customer-experienced outcomes, not component specs. For example: "real-world range ≥ X km / Y mi", "10–80 % in ≤ N min", "cooler fits N × 0.75 l bottles", "seat feels cool within N min". Battery kWh, compressor type or supplier would be out. Judging signal: "Customer value over engineering specs / regulation / business case."
- **Scope tensions already open in the brief:**
  - Driver assistance: the experience is in, safety performance is out (Q-016).
  - The "Business" dimension may only use market volume and rough effort, with no business-case math.
  - Platform feasibility versus "architecture" being out of scope (Q-010, resolved by D-030 as non-blocking).
- **Mentor input:** balance across markets (climate, usage, culture); extract *future* requirements; the process is ~2 years with re-prioritization; use the BMW Group Report 2025 as strategy context.

## 2. Requirement model and architecture (pre-rebuild, superseded for new screens by D-043)

`/Users/atahankilic/Documents/ehl-munich-final/foundation/documents/requirement-model.md` (v4) and `/Users/atahankilic/Documents/ehl-munich-final/foundation/documents/architecture.md`.

**Fields:**
- `id` REQ-0001
- `targets`: derivative × market, each with `realization` = carry_over / platform_wide / derivative_specific / market_variant / package, and its own score, priority and fit
- `horizon`: today / at_successor_launch
- `kano_class` + `kano_drift`
- `title` / `description`
- `category`: Exterior · Interior · Comfort & Space · Infotainment & Digital · Driving Experience · Powertrain (as experienced) · Range & Charging · Driver Assistance (as experienced) · Variants & Packages · Design & Quality Perception
- `target_metric` / `acceptance_criteria`: just "Measurable where possible". Each is a single text column on `requirement`, with no structure, no value/unit, and no benchmark link.
- `linked_findings`, `fit_checks` (brand / segment / market / feasibility), score / breakdown / priority, rationale, evidence_level, assumptions / uncertainties, conflicting_evidence
- `status`: proposed → in_review → approved / rejected / deferred; challenged goes back to proposed. The AI may only create requirements in `proposed`.

**Evidence levels (deterministic, per target):**
- E1: ≥ 20 verbatims from ≥ 2 channels, plus a study gap or a T1/T2 web finding
- E2: ≥ 15 verbatims, or ≥ 3 verbatims + study / web, or study + web
- E3: any evidence
- E4: assumptions only

**Scoring v1 (D-029), amended by D-038 (score-v3):**
- Weights: customer voice 30, satisfaction gap 15, market volume 15, competitive pressure 15, future relevance 15, portfolio leverage 10.
- Confidence multiplier: E1 1.0 / E2 0.92 / E3 0.75 / E4 0.5 (the D-038 values).
- Modifiers: market fit +2 / −5 / −10; effort S 0 / M −3 / L −6.
- Bands: Must ≥ 60, Should ≥ 45.

**What the D-043 rebuild supersedes:**
- New screens read only D-043 tables (`insight`, `theme`, `evidence_edge`, `req_area`). The old `requirement` / `requirement_target` / `finding` / linker tables are kept "for history".
- Scoring has "not been rebuilt for the D-043 pipeline yet" (D-046).
- Current state in `data/app.db`: `req_area` holds 15 / 37 areas at cp1 (runs 11 and 13) and 41 at cp2 (run 16). Each area has title, need, kind (improve / keep / emerging / quality), why_now, `open_questions_json` (≤ 3 drafting questions) and `metrics_json` (coverage, evidence, market).
- `elicit.py` (`/Users/atahankilic/Documents/ehl-munich-final/src/bmw_req/structure/elicit.py`) is written but not run. Its Draft schema is: title, statement, decision_type (add_feature / raise_capability / change_design / keep_strength / package_variant / market_variant), today_status (standard / optional / package / not_offered / unknown), `metric{name, unit, method}`, targets[line, market, rationale, evidence_ids], horizon + horizon_year, kano, evidence_ids, trend_ids, assumptions.
- **Elicit has no target value, no acceptance criteria, no benchmark reference, no coupling/links between requirements, and no domain grouping beyond the theme/category.** That is the gap your layer fills.
- Code checks in elicit: a future horizon needs a dated trend edge; each market target needs evidence from its own market; cited ids must come from the theme's edges.

## 3. Decisions (`/Users/atahankilic/Documents/ehl-munich-final/foundation/DECISIONS.md`)

- **D-012 (future needs):** a projection step turns predecessor findings + competitor trajectory + trends + market profile into the need at successor launch (3–5 yr). Each requirement carries a horizon and a Kano class with expected drift (delighter → basic, e.g. OTA, ADAS in China). Projections are tagged E4/assumption unless current evidence backs them. *For definition: target levels at launch must be projected, not set to today's best-in-class, and the projection must be marked as an assumption.*
- **D-028 (derivation v3):** sol, per vehicle line, proposes only NEW requirements, using top pain/want/strength findings, study, web, market profiles, brand guardrails and sales. Drafts without validated evidence are dropped. Market targeting must be evidence-based (v2 put nearly everything on every market, with effort mostly L). Wave drafts are consolidated across lines. Afterwards a luna linker attaches study and web evidence per target market.
- **D-029 (scoring v1):** the formula above. Missing factors are renormalized and shown as evidence gaps. Brand fit is a gate only. Weights are PM-editable and versioned. A PM-confirmed priority that a later run would change becomes a `change_proposal` with the factor-level cause.
- **D-038 (product decisions):**
  - A requirement must state a tradeable `product_decision`. "X must work reliably" is a defect and goes to the Quality hand-over.
  - **Strict merging:** drafts are merged only if one product decision satisfies all of them **and the metrics measure the same thing**.
  - Markets without their own comments borrow ×0.5 and are capped, unless they have both a study gap and competitor pressure.
  - Kano-basic requirements get one priority across all markets.
  - *For definition: one metric per requirement, and coupled-but-different metrics become links, not merges.*
- **D-043 (structure rebuild):** classify (≈45-aspect taxonomy, with a `benchmark` field: none / previous_bmw / competitor / phone_tech) → cluster → contextualize (insights, themes, typed `evidence_edge`s such as supports, contradicts, competes_with, trend_for, available_as_option, context) → areas. "This step structures, it does not draft requirements". Drafting (elicit) is the next step and was explicitly not run. Every stage is a `checkpoint_run`, and cp2 builds on cp1.
- **D-046 (sales):**
  - BMW's sales file is a labelled relative weight only (share per line × market, "internal and stylized (Q-015)"), never a trend.
  - Trends come only from cited public research items visible at the checkpoint.
  - Differences > 25 % are flagged (5 Series US +188 %, China −35 %).
  - Areas carry `metrics.market`, which is meant for later prioritization.
- **D-047 (evidence pool):** `web` and `reference` items join `research` as evidence candidates (K 10 → 14). `relink` writes a new contextualize run. Brand, market-profile, platform and plant reference tables are "kept for the requirement-drafting step".

## 4. Quantitative benchmarks

**Where they live:**
- **`/Users/atahankilic/Documents/ehl-munich-final/research/checkpoints/checkpoints.json`:** 1,028 items under `{checkpoints, items, gaps}`. Schema is in `research/checkpoints/SCHEMA.md`, and per-topic raw files are in `research/checkpoints/raw/*.json` (bmw, china_*, consumer_studies, ev_challengers, markets, policy_macro, premium_competitors, segment_sales, tech_trends).
  - Item fields: id, checkpoint (2026-01 / 2026-07), kind, region, entity, segment, powertrain, metric, period_covered, `value`, `unit`, yoy_pct, headline, driver, customer_relevance, pair_key, source{url, publisher, published_at, trust_tier}, quote (verified on the page), notes.
  - It is mostly sales. Units: units 533, pct 200, points 79, **km only 7, kw only 8**. Spec facts often have `unit: null` and the number sits in the headline or quote.
  - The same items are in the DB as `source_item(kind='research')` (T1 415 / T2 405 / T3 208), with the schema fields in `meta_json` and visibility in `source_item.checkpoint` (cp1 / cp2).
- **Web-agent findings:** `source_item(kind='web')`, 219 items (T1 89 / T2 128 / T3 2). `meta_json.evidence_type` is competitor_feature 76, customer_expectation 36, review_criticism 25, competitor_sales 24, market_profile 21, review_praise 19, market_trend 18; plus `meta_json.category`, competitor, models, quote_verified. Numbers appear only in the free `text`.
- **Reference layer:** `source_item(kind='reference')`, 96 items. They come from `foundation/documents/competitor-landscape.md` (S-keys, with `meta_json.unverified`) and `portfolio-reference.md`. Facts are free text.
- **`/Users/atahankilic/Documents/ehl-munich-final/foundation/documents/competitor-landscape.md`:** spec benchmarks live in the table rows (lines 29–74) and the trends table (lines 112–116). `(U)` marks unverified facts. `portfolio-reference.md` is mostly plants, platforms and sales, with almost no spec numbers.
- **There is no structured "spec benchmark" table** (attribute, value, unit, model, market, test cycle). A target-setting agent would have to query by aspect / category and extract numbers from text. For research items it can use `json_extract(meta_json,'$.unit') IN ('km','kw')` or LIKE on the text.

**Examples (id / location, value, source and tier):**
1. `bmw-ix3-lwb-range-jul-2026`: China iX3 LWB, 919 km CLTC, 400 km in 10 min. CarNewsChina, T2, cp2. Also web `web:24108a39e223`: >900 km CLTC, up to 400 kW, >400 km in 10 min, BMW PressClub China, T1.
2. `bmw-7-series-lci-apr-2026`: i7 facelift up to 452 mi (stored as value 452, unit "km", which is a unit inconsistency). BMW PressClub UK, T1. competitor-landscape line 29: 17.9″ screen, 700–728 km WLTP (U), DC 195–250 kW.
3. `bmw-i3-reveal-mar-2026`: Neue Klasse i3, up to 900 km WLTP. Evo India, T3.
4. competitor-landscape S13 (`source_item` ref `competitor-landscape.md#S13`): Mercedes CLA, 792 km WLTP, 320 kW DC, +325 km in 10 min.
5. `web:3e4ac59f84ed`: electric Mercedes C-Class, 762 km WLTP, +325 km in 10 min. Mercedes-Benz Media, T1, 2026-07-28.
6. `byd-flash-charging-1000kw` / `-1500kw`: BYD 1,000 kW, 400 km in 5 min (cp1), then 1,500 kW (cp2). CnEVPost, T2. `cn-megawatt-chargers-jul-2026`: Hongqi 10–70 % in 3 min 41 s, T2.
7. `mercedes-glc-ev-cn-jul-2026`: GLC EV China, 3,027 mm wheelbase, 39.1″ screen, RMB 338k. CnEVPost, T2.
8. `web:0416497e1962`: BMW 7 Series 31.3″ rear Theatre Screen vs. S-Class 2 × 13.6″. Autocar India, T2. `web:00d0318e1f9f`: Genesis G80 27″ OLED standard, T1.
9. `jdp-cn-iqs-2026-seat-ventilation`: seat ventilation fitment in China rose 14 % → 36 %. J.D. Power, T2. `web:40a9c6d56935`: NIO ET7 rear ventilation + hot-stone massage standard, T1. `web:429492370233`: NIO ET5 +75 mm rear cushion length, T1.
10. Fridge / cooler: competitor-landscape lines 58, 68, 74, 102 say AITO M9 / S-Class / S800 have a fridge, M9 a 32″ projector. **There is no capacity figure (litres or bottles) anywhere.**
11. `bmw-motorway-assistant-r171-approval`: BMW hands-off driving up to 130 km/h in Europe (UN R171). BMW, T1. `cn-l2-penetration-2026-miit`: L2 in 70 % of new China cars in 2026, NOA > 30 %, Xinhua, T2. `china-urban-noa-penetration-2025-caam`: 15.1 %, T3. `mercedes-drive-pilot-paused`: L3 dropped, electrive, T2.
12. OTA: `deloitte-2026-cn-ota-wtp` (only 7 % of Chinese unwilling to pay), `deloitte-2026-de-ota-wtp` (40 % of Germans unwilling), `deloitte-2026-ota-keep-longer` (52 % of US would keep the car longer). All Deloitte, T2.
13. Range concern: `deloitte-2026-de-range-concern` 49 %, `deloitte-2026-us-range-concern` 47%. Deloitte, T2.
14. HMI: `sp-global-hmi-combo-preference`, 48 % prefer touchscreen + physical controls, S&P, T2. `jdp-us-iqs-2026-infotainment-premium` 38.3 PP100; `jdp-us-iqs-2026-distraction` 46 %. J.D. Power, T2.
15. 0–100 km/h: only Denza Z9 3.4 s (competitor-landscape line 60). The option-list ingest has **no** WLTP / range / boot-volume values (0 matches; "Technische Werte" was not ingested).

**Gaps:**
- No boot volume (litres) for any competitor.
- Almost no 10–80 % charging times for BMW's direct rivals.
- No cooler capacity.
- No seat-ventilation performance or speed.
- No 0–100 km/h times for BMW lines.
- No range figures in US EPA miles except the i7.
- Mixed test cycles (CLTC / WLTP / EPA) would need normalising.

## 5. Customer study as a current-performance baseline (`/Users/atahankilic/Documents/ehl-munich-final/foundation/documents/data-inventory.md` §2)

**Stored in table `study_metric`:** columns source_item_id, vehicle_model_id, market_code, item, scale, mean, top2, bottom3, net, z_within_column, rank_within_column, n_items_in_column.

**CN/EU (`scale mean_10`):** 37 categories for G68 CN, G70 CN, F70 EU, G60 EU and G70 EU. Means are ~6.5–9.9; the scale (0–10 or 1–10) is unconfirmed (Q-006). There are no sample sizes.
- Categories: overall, styling, interior quality, equipment level, controls/displays, smartphone integration, infotainment features + ease of use, navigation, seating comfort, storage, acceleration, roadholding, efficiency, braking, ride, front/rear roominess, luggage loading + capacity, ingress/egress, HVAC, build quality, quietness, driving position, connected services, interior versatility, and more.
- Examples:
  - Luggage capacity: F70 EU 7.07 (z −2.27), G70 CN 7.66 (z −1.34)
  - Ease of loading: G68 CN 7.25 (z −2.15)
  - Efficiency: G60 EU 7.45 (z −1.17)
  - Seating comfort: G70 EU 9.29

**US (`scale dist_7`):** 103 granular questions for G60 and G70 only, with mean / top2 / bottom3 / net. The base is a share, not a respondent count.
- Examples: comfort of 2nd row seat, G60 5.27 (z −0.35) vs. G70 6.24; seat materials; roominess per row; cupholders; cargo; climate; audio; controls intuitiveness; NVH.

**Caveats:**
- **No dedicated "range" or "charging" item** (efficiency is the closest).
- No F70 in the US and no China verbatims.
- CN/EU and US scales are not comparable.
- The data works as a relative "how good today" baseline via within-column z, not as an absolute target.

## 6. Option price lists (German)

**Ingest:** `source_item(kind='option_list')`, T1, cp1. F70 159 rows, G60 142, G70 157. One row per equipment line. `ref` looks like `F70_OptionList.PDF#p10:<slug>`. `meta_json` holds name_de, name_en, `category` (requirement taxonomy), `availability` (standard / optional / package), package_name, option_code, applies_to, price_eur, section (standard_equipment / model_equipment / package / options / wheels), page, line_verified, and market_note ("German-market list. Equipment for US/CN…" is an assumption). Aspects are mapped in `source_aspect`. D-043 contextualize links them to themes as `available_as_option` edges.

**As a "what exists today" baseline, it works for equipment presence per model:**
- G60: "Active seat ventilation, front" (package); 12.3″ + 14.9″ display combination; Curved Display; HUD.
- G70: active seat ventilation front and rear, massage front and rear (package); 3D HUD standard.
- F70: 10.25″ + 10.7″ display, HUD (package).
- No cooler / fridge entry was found in any list.

**Limits:**
- Germany only.
- Many package items have no price.
- No performance values: range, boot volume, charging and 0–100 were not ingested. They exist in the PDFs' "Technische Werte" section, but under the confidentiality rule they would need a new ingest.
- It feeds elicit's `today_status` (standard / optional / package / not_offered) but not a quantitative baseline.

- Code checks in elicit: a future horizon needs a dated trend edge; each market target needs evidence from its own market; cited ids must come from the theme's edges.

## 3. Decisions (`/Users/atahankilic/Documents/ehl-munich-final/foundation/DECISIONS.md`)

- **D-012 (future needs):** a projection step turns predecessor findings + competitor trajectory + trends + market profile into the need at successor launch (3–5 yr). Each requirement carries a horizon and a Kano class with expected drift (delighter → basic, e.g. OTA, ADAS in China). Projections are tagged E4/assumption unless current evidence backs them. *For definition: target levels at launch must be projected, not set to today's best-in-class, and the projection must be marked as an assumption.*
- **D-028 (derivation v3):** sol, per vehicle line, proposes only NEW requirements, using top pain/want/strength findings, study, web, market profiles, brand guardrails and sales. Drafts without validated evidence are dropped. Market targeting must be evidence-based (v2 put nearly everything on every market, with effort mostly L). Wave drafts are consolidated across lines. Afterwards a luna linker attaches study and web evidence per target market.
- **D-029 (scoring v1):** the formula above. Missing factors are renormalized and shown as evidence gaps. Brand fit is a gate only. Weights are PM-editable and versioned. A PM-confirmed priority that a later run would change becomes a `change_proposal` with the factor-level cause.
- **D-038 (product decisions):**
  - A requirement must state a tradeable `product_decision`. "X must work reliably" is a defect and goes to the Quality hand-over.
  - **Strict merging:** drafts are merged only if one product decision satisfies all of them **and the metrics measure the same thing**.
  - Markets without their own comments borrow ×0.5 and are capped, unless they have both a study gap and competitor pressure.
  - Kano-basic requirements get one priority across all markets.
  - *For definition: one metric per requirement, and coupled-but-different metrics become links, not merges.*
- **D-043 (structure rebuild):** classify (≈45-aspect taxonomy, with a `benchmark` field: none / previous_bmw / competitor / phone_tech) → cluster → contextualize (insights, themes, typed `evidence_edge`s such as supports, contradicts, competes_with, trend_for, available_as_option, context) → areas. "This step structures, it does not draft requirements". Drafting (elicit) is the next step and was explicitly not run. Every stage is a `checkpoint_run`, and cp2 builds on cp1.
- **D-046 (sales):**
  - BMW's sales file is a labelled relative weight only (share per line × market, "internal and stylized (Q-015)"), never a trend.
  - Trends come only from cited public research items visible at the checkpoint.
  - Differences > 25 % are flagged (5 Series US +188 %, China −35 %).
  - Areas carry `metrics.market`, which is meant for later prioritization.
- **D-047 (evidence pool):** `web` and `reference` items join `research` as evidence candidates (K 10 → 14). `relink` writes a new contextualize run. Brand, market-profile, platform and plant reference tables are "kept for the requirement-drafting step".
